question: What is the main goal of taking and handing over on the ward?

options.A: To transfer patient care responsibilities safely between shifts
options.B: To replace formal written patient medical records completely
options.C: To give nurses a chance to socialise before starting work
options.D: To allow doctors to check if nurses are doing their jobs

explanation: Handover makes sure that important care details move securely from the outgoing nurse to the incoming one, so no patient is left unprotected! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h1)

question: When you take over a new shift, what do you accept regarding your assigned patients?

options.A: Financial responsibility for their hospital bills
options.B: Legal and professional accountability for their care
options.C: The obligation to discharge them by the end of the day
options.D: Full ownership of all past medical errors made by doctors

explanation: Taking over patients means you are now officially responsible for watching over them and giving them proper care during your shift. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is one primary purpose of giving a shift report?

options.A: Providing a detailed history of the nurse's personal life
options.B: Eliminating the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: Reducing the total number of working hours for hospital staff
options.D: Ensuring continuity of care across different nursing shifts

explanation: The shift report acts like a bridge between shifts, keeping patient care smooth and uninterrupted. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h2)

question: How does a good shift report help an incoming nurse manage their time?

options.A: By automatically completing all routine charting in advance
options.B: By stopping any new admissions from arriving on the ward
options.C: By allowing the nurse to sleep during the first hour of the shift
options.D: By highlighting unstable patients so urgent tasks are prioritized

explanation: Knowing who needs attention right now helps you plan your time wisely and tackle the most urgent needs first. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h2)

question: Where did traditional verbal handovers usually take place?

options.A: Inside the hospital pharmacy during medication restocking
options.B: In a conference room or nursing station away from the patient
options.C: Directly inside the patient's bathroom while they shower
options.D: At the hospital gates as staff members arrive for work

explanation: Traditionally, reports were given away from the clinical area, though nowadays we love doing them right at the bedside! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is a major downside of relying only on a written handover book without talking?

options.A: It is too expensive for a standard hospital ward to maintain
options.B: It lacks the interactive opportunity to ask questions or clarify details
options.C: It instantly deletes all nursing notes after eight hours
options.D: It forces patients to listen to private staff conversations

explanation: Writing is great, but nothing beats live chat where you can ask questions immediately if something about a patient's condition is confusing. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is a must-share piece of information during a patient handover?

options.A: The brand name of the hospital bed mattress
options.C: The personal phone number of the patient's relative
options.D: Current vital signs and recent lab results

explanation: Vitals and lab values give a clear, quick picture of how stable the patient is right now. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why must you mention pending lab tests or investigations during a shift report?

options.A: To prove to the hospital management that tests are expensive
options.B: So the patient can decide whether to cancel the appointment
options.C: So the incoming nurse can monitor preparation and follow up on results
options.D: To ensure the laboratory staff receive extra break time

explanation: Tests often need special preparation before and tracking after, which becomes the job of the incoming shift. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h4)

question: What does the letter 'A' stand for in the SBAR communication framework?
explanation: In SBAR, 'A' stands for Assessment, representing your professional evaluation of the patient's current clinical findings. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h5)

question: A nurse tells a doctor: 'The patient's blood pressure is dropping and urine output has stopped.' Which part of SBAR is this?
explanation: Describing what is happening right at this exact moment is the 'Situation' part of SBAR. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of doing handovers right at the patient's bedside?

options.A: It prevents doctors from ever entering the patient's room
options.B: It completely removes the need for any written nursing notes
options.C: It reduces the total number of required vital sign checks
options.D: It allows patients to hear their care plan and ask questions

explanation: Bedside handovers make patients part of their own healing journey and help catch any mistakes early! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h6)

question: How should a nurse protect a patient's dignity during a bedside handover?

options.A: Speak in a very loud voice so everyone in the hallway can hear
options.B: Ask all family members to permanently leave the hospital ward
options.C: Ensure privacy curtains are drawn and sensitive details are discussed discreetly
options.D: Refuse to let the patient look at their own medical chart

explanation: Always draw privacy curtains and keep your voice soft and respectful when talking about private health matters. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h6)

question: Where is it completely inappropriate to discuss confidential patient handover details?

options.A: At the patient's bedside with privacy curtains drawn
options.B: In a public hospital cafeteria or open hallway
options.C: During a structured team conference meeting
options.D: Inside a private, closed nursing station room

explanation: Public spots let unauthorized people overhear private medical information, which breaks patient confidentiality. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why is accurate handover documentation legally important for you as a nurse?

options.A: It prevents the nursing council from inspecting the hospital
options.B: It serves as evidence that patient care and responsibilities were properly transferred
options.C: It guarantees that the nurse will never be questioned by a doctor
options.D: It allows the hospital to charge higher fees for room maintenance

explanation: Clear notes protect you legally by proving you handed over patient duties responsibly and professionally. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which of these is a common challenge that ruins a good nursing handover?

options.C: Having too many standardized reporting templates
options.D: Patients being fully awake and cooperative

explanation: When people are tired and the ward is noisy, it's super easy to miss crucial details during report. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h8)

question: A ward always has rushed handovers because staff arrive late. What is the best way to fix this?

options.A: Allow outgoing nurses to leave before the incoming shift arrives
options.B: Cancel all shift handovers permanently and rely on text messages
options.C: Reduce the amount of patient care required during the day
options.D: Implement strict arrival policies and use a structured handover checklist

explanation: Using a checklist alongside clear punctuality rules keeps handovers organized, quick, and right on track! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h8)
